title: correlation-id-and-endpoint-dimensions-jsonl-logs-for-openai-shim
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Add correlation-id propagation and per-endpoint metric dimensions; emit newline-delimited JSON logs for streaming/tool events; compatibility mapping for OpenAI-style request headers. This improves root-cause tracing for streaming drops and per-route cost attribution.
description:
Motivation: Users running streaming and function-calling workloads need reliable correlation across gateway, runtime and SDKs to tie partial streams and tool invocations back to a single request. Existing observability was sparse for streaming slices and tool/function calls.
Goals: 1) propagate a stable correlation id (header: X-Correlation-ID) across the OpenAI compatibility shim and runtime, 2) attach endpoint and variant dimensions to HTTP metrics and Prometheus labels so per-route cost/latency is visible, 3) emit structured JSONL logs for streaming chunks and tool call boundaries so log ingestion can reconstruct full interactions, 4) avoid changing public user-facing API semantics but provide compatibility mappings for common OpenAI headers.
What changed:
- Gateway: map incoming OpenAI style request headers (e.g. OpenAI-Client-Request-Id) to X-Correlation-ID if present; if none found, generate a v4 UUID early in the request path. Ensure header is passed to downstream runtime and to internal async event bus.
- Runtime: attach correlation_id to all emitted span tags and to streaming chunk events. Streaming fragment logs now include fields: correlation_id, stream_offset, partial_text, model_variant, route_name, and sequence_token when available. Logs are emitted as newline-delimited JSON to the structured logger.
- Metrics: per-endpoint metrics include new label endpoint=/<route> and variant=<model-variant>. Added a lightweight mapping in metrics exporter to avoid cardinality explosion: only include variant for routes marked as high_variance in route config.
- SDK shim (OpenAI-compat): expose correlation id in response metadata under top-level "correlation_id" for quick access in SDKs and examples. Also preserve compatibility headers for downstream user code.
- E2E tests: added deterministic test for correlation propagation across gateway->runtime->function-hook cycle, and an integration test that asserts JSONL structure for streaming partials.
- Docs: updated observability.md with examples for searching logs by correlation_id and configuring endpoint dimensions.
Implementation notes: conservative approach to labels to prevent high tag cardinality. UUID generated once per inbound HTTP request. When requests are retried by the client via the compatibility shim, the shim preserves the original correlation id unless explicitly overridden.
Backwards compatibility: no request body semantics were changed; header mapping is additive.
Rollout plan: feature gated behind FF_TELEMETRY_CORRELATION (default on for staging, opt-in for production rollout).
commits_summary: 1) generate/carry correlation id at gateway and map OpenAI headers -> X-Correlation-ID; 2) wire id through runtime spans and streaming emitter; 3) JSONL streaming log formatter and tests; 4) metrics exporter labels for endpoint/variant with cardinality guard; 5) openai-shim exposes correlation_id in SDK responses; 6) docs and examples update
review_comments: Evan Liu: Nice work. Question: are we sure we won't accidentally increase Prometheus cardinality when variant changes per request? Please add guard logic or sampling.
Priya Shah: Added guard. exporter now checks route config high_variance flag and only labels variant when true. Also added unit test to ensure labels length bounded.
Marco Diaz: The JSONL schema looks good but add an explicit timestamp and sequence number for each chunk to make reassembly deterministic.
Priya Shah: Added timestamp and sequence_token. Updated tests accordingly.
Ava Thompson: Can we document how this interacts with existing request IDs in downstream services? It confused our SREs in dev.
author_responses: Priya Shah: Added a note in observability.md recommending using correlation_id as the canonical trace key; included a migration snippet for downstream services to read X-Correlation-ID.
Priya Shah: Feature flag added to configs/feature_flags.yaml to control rollout.
merge_details: Merged via squash on 2026-02-24 after approvals from Evan Liu and Marco Diaz. No conflicts. Changelog entry added to RELEASE_NOTES.md.
testing_notes: New tests cover gateway mapping, runtime propagation, JSONL log schema, and metrics exporter label safeguards. Manual verification performed on staging with a streaming demo: search by correlation_id returned the full session and associated tool call logs.
notes_for_ops: When enabling FF_TELEMETRY_CORRELATION in production, monitor Prometheus series count for the first 24h. If series growth > 5% for endpoints, flip flag for the affected service and file ENG-1989.
security_considerations: Correlation IDs are UUID4 and do not contain PII. We avoid echoing user-supplied headers verbatim in logs — OpenAI-compat mapped headers are normalized and validated before emission.
how_to_use_examples: SDK note: response.metadata.correlation_id is available in Python and TS SDKs under response.metadata['correlation_id']
